title: Resource‐efficient potato fertilization in acid Inceptisols using a soil‐test crop response framework: Mineral‐input savings, field validation, and screening upstream urea‐manufacturing implications
content:
Abstract

Efficient fertilizer management in acid soils requires decision frameworks that translate soil-test variability into crop-specific nutrient demand while minimizing unnecessary mineral inputs. This study developed and field-validated Soil Test Crop Response (STCR) fertilizer prescriptions for potato under acid Inceptisol conditions in Meghalaya, India. A three-phase field program conducted during 2022–2024 established fertility gradients, derived crop nutrient-response parameters, and independently validated STCR-NPK and integrated plant nutrient supply (STCR-IPNS) prescriptions at target yields of 100, 125, and 150 q ha−1. Nutrient requirements for producing one quintal of tubers were 0.56 kg N, 0.26 kg P, and 0.93 kg K. Across the prescription matrix, FYM integration reduced mineral-N demand by 23.76–23.80 kg N ha−1 and K2O demand by 7.0–7.1 kg ha−1, while realized P2O5 savings ranged from 0 to 32.7 kg ha−1 depending on soil-test P and target yield. Aggregate realized mineral nutrient-equivalent savings ranged from 30.76 to 63.60 kg ha−1. All six targeted-yield treatments remained within ±10% of prescribed yields, with a mean absolute target deviation of 6.04%, and STCR-IPNS maintained tuber yield relative to STCR-NPK. Mineral-N displacement corresponded to 51.65–51.74 kg urea-equivalent ha−1 and a screening estimate of 79.7–97.4 kg CO2-eq ha−1 of gross upstream urea-manufacturing burden potentially avoided. This indicator excludes other fertilizer-system and field emissions. Overall, STCR-IPNS maintained predefined potato yield targets while reducing external mineral-fertilizer demand and supporting resource-efficient nutrient management in acidic soils. The framework supports precise fertilizer targeting, mineral-resource conservation, and integration of organic nutrient credits in acid-soil potato production systems.
